answer: Samagna (also known as BanaSetu) is a digital procurement and batch traceability ledger for minor forest produce. It connects primary tribal collectors, self-help groups, aggregation centres, and warehouses with verified weighment and fair pricing records.

questions: Is this affiliated with Government of Odisha?
Is this a pilot or production system?
answer: Samagna is an independent digital demonstration platform and is not an official government agency. All payments, DBT disbursements, and royalty figures shown in this environment are simulated pilot demonstrations.

questions: How do you calculate collector payment?
How is money calculated for my produce?
answer: Collector payments are calculated as: Net Weight (Certified Gross minus Tare) multiplied by the Approved Minimum Support Price (MSP) rate per kilogram. The assistant never computes custom figures; check your latest receipt for exact numbers.

questions: Are platform fees deducted from collectors?
Is commission taken from my MSP?
Can government royalty reduce collector payment?
answer: No. Platform fees, buyer commissions, and government service royalties are strictly institutional charges and are never deducted from primary gatherers. Forest collectors receive 100% of their statutory MSP entitlement.

questions: What does the batch QR code show?
What is printed on the sack tag?
answer: Every verified batch receives a unique QR code linked to its provenance record. Scanning it reveals the origin district, aggregation centre, moisture percentage, and custody checkpoints while protecting gatherer personal data.

questions: What is gross weight and tare weight?
answer: Gross weight is the total weight of the produce plus sack. Tare weight is the empty weight of the container (typically 0.1 kg to 1.5 kg). Net weight is Gross minus Tare, representing the actual certified produce being purchased.

questions: Can I use Samagna without internet?
What happens when there is no network?
How to sync records when online?
answer: Samagna works offline using a local encrypted database. Weighment receipts and pickup requests save to your device immediately and sync automatically to the central registry when network connectivity is restored.

questions: Why is my data not syncing?
answer: Unsent records remain queued if network connectivity is absent or the server session has expired. Check the Sync Status drawer at the top of your screen to inspect pending items and trigger manual synchronization.

questions: What does a sync conflict mean?
Why is my record flagged as conflict?
answer: A sync conflict occurs if a batch record was modified by another officer or quarantined due to moisture/weight variance. Conflicted items are safely preserved on your device and flagged for District Supervisor review.

questions: How do I take photo of scale readout?
answer: Tap the Camera button on the weighment screen to photograph the produce and electronic scale readout. Photos captured offline are compressed and stored locally, then uploaded when connectivity is restored.

questions: How do I contact my SHG facilitator?
answer: Your registered SHG facilitator assists with pickup requests and initial bagging at your village aggregation point. You can view your designated facilitator under your Collector profile tab.

questions: Can you give current prices offline?
answer: The assistant can confirm current rates only when online. When offline, please consult your latest printed receipt or open the cached Rates tab on your dashboard for the latest synchronized rate card.

questions: How do B2B wholesale orders work?
How can businesses buy forest produce in bulk?
What is the wholesale procurement process?
How do I submit an RFQ?
Can manufacturers purchase Mahua or Sal Seeds?
answer: Institutional buyers, manufacturers, and wholesalers can browse certified forest produce lots on the B2B Trade portal (/trade), request bulk quotations (RFQ), and access verified origin certificates with lab test reports.

questions: How does the retail store work?
Can consumers buy packaged forest honey?
What products are available in the store?
Where can I buy retail forest products?
answer: Consumers can purchase sustainably harvested, laboratory-tested forest produce including wild forest honey, organic amla candy, and herbal powders directly through the Samagna Store (/store) with doorstep delivery.

questions: What are the moisture limits for produce?
What is certified quality for Mahua?
Why is produce checked for moisture?
What is Fair Average Quality FAQ?
answer: Each produce has strict quality standards: Dried Mahua Flowers allow a maximum 12% moisture and 1.5% transit shrinkage; Sal Tree Seeds allow 10% moisture and 1.2% shrinkage; Chironji allows 8% moisture. Batches exceeding limits are dried before final bagging.

questions: How does LABHA protect tribal gatherers?
answer: Under the Government of Odisha LABHA (Laghu Bana Jatiya Dradya Kraya) scheme, 100% of the Minimum Support Price (MSP) is disbursed directly to tribal gatherers with 0% platform commission or intermediary deduction. Samagna provides digital traceability to uphold this statutory mandate.
sourceRef: Government of Odisha LABHA Scheme Guidelines

questions: What happens if there is a weight discrepancy?
How do I file a grievance?
answer: If aggregation centre weight diverges beyond allowable tolerance from initial field weighment, the lot is placed in Quarantine Discrepancy status. The District DPO/Supervisor Admin reviews scale calibration and evidence photos before resolution, ensuring primary collectors are protected from arbitrary deductions.
